provenance.notes: Leaned on how walk-in patients choose: wait time, distance and open now, plus employers as a second buyer. Nothing on the site assesses symptoms. Unsure on the live wait-time feed and employer portal ranges; both depend on the clinic's queue and records systems.

pageStructurePlus.section: Live wait times and save-my-spot check-in
pageStructurePlus.contains: The current wait at each urgent care clinic, online check-in that holds a place in line, a text when it's nearly their turn, and a note that sicker patients may be seen first
pageStructurePlus.why: Walk-in patients choose on wait and distance, often from a phone in the car park. Showing both is what wins the visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A plain list of what the clinics see and what they don't, with a prominent instruction to call the local emergency number for severe symptoms, all approved by the medical director
pageStructurePlus.why: Unsure patients look for this before driving anywhere. A clear, careful answer earns trust and sends real emergencies to the right place.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Self-pay ranges for a basic visit, x-ray, stitches and common tests as [price] placeholders the clinic confirms, plus insurance accepted at each clinic
pageStructurePlus.why: Patients without cover, or with high out-of-pocket costs, compare clinics on price before they walk in. A clear range stops them driving elsewhere.

pageStructurePlus.section: Services by clinic: x-ray, lab and stitches
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which clinics have on-site x-ray, lab testing, stitches and splinting, children's hours and step-free access, shown as filters on the location finder
pageStructurePlus.why: A parent whose child fell needs the nearest clinic with x-ray, not just the nearest clinic. One wasted trip loses that family.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Work injury care, pre-employment physicals and drug screening, how employers open an account, and how work-status forms reach the employer with the worker's consent
pageStructurePlus.why: Employers are repeat buyers who pick one clinic network for every worker. They decide on convenience, paperwork and clinic coverage.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What a video visit can handle, its hours and [price], how to start one from a phone, and when the clinic will ask the patient to come in instead
pageStructurePlus.why: Some patients would rather not leave home at all. A clear start page keeps them with the clinic instead of a national app.

designDirections.name: Wait Board
designDirections.bestFor: Networks of walk-in clinics where the live wait time and the nearest open location are the whole decision
designDirections.headlineSample: See the wait at every {City} urgent care clinic
designDirections.whyItFits: Black on white with a single red and a mono face for numbers makes wait times read like a departures board. Each clinic is a card with its wait and a check-in button.

designDirections.name: Save My Spot
designDirections.bestFor: Groups selling online check-in, self-pay prices and virtual visits from one booking-first home page
designDirections.headlineSample: Check in online at a {City} walk-in clinic
designDirections.whyItFits: Chosen over the family's warm cream combo: someone deciding in a car park needs bright, clinical clarity. Cobalt and a neutral grotesque read as quick and trustworthy.

designDirections.name: Employer Health Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Larger urgent care groups with occupational health contracts, employer accounts and clinics across a region
designDirections.headlineSample: Work injury and urgent care across {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Deep green and a classical serif say established and dependable to an HR manager comparing clinic networks, while the patient path stays one click away.

openers.line: Your urgent care listings show opening hours but nothing about the wait. A parent with a feverish child picks the clinic that shows a wait time on their phone.
openers.hook: Check each clinic's listing and the site for any wait time. If there's none anywhere, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Live wait times for every urgent care clinic: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to save a spot at your walk-in clinics online. Most people would rather wait on their own sofa than in a waiting room full of coughing strangers.
openers.hook: Look for a check-in or 'save my spot' link on the site and listings. Note if it's missing at every clinic.
openers.linkLine: Online check-in with a text when it's nearly your turn: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your clinics close at different times, but the site lists hours in one block. At eight in the evening, someone has to work out which urgent care is still open.
openers.hook: Compare the hours on two clinic listings with the site. Note any that differ.
openers.linkLine: An open-now finder across your walk-in clinics: {demo-link}

openers.line: Reviews keep asking what an urgent care visit costs without insurance. A self-pay price range on the site answers that before someone drives to a competitor who shows one.
openers.hook: Search their reviews and comments for 'price', 'cost' or 'self-pay'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Self-pay prices for each urgent care service: {demo-link}

openers.line: A few reviews mention people unsure whether to come to your clinic or go to the emergency department. A careful page on what your urgent care sees would help them decide before they drive.
openers.hook: Look for reviews from people sent on to an emergency department or unsure where to go. Never comment on a patient's case.
openers.linkLine: A clear 'urgent care or emergency' page for your clinics: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing mentions work injury care and pre-employment physicals, but there's nothing for an employer to open an account. HR managers pick the clinic network that makes that easy.
openers.hook: Check the listing and site for occupational health or employer wording. Note whether there's a form.
openers.linkLine: An employer page for your occupational health clinic services: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw your group is hiring nurses and providers for more than one clinic. There's no careers page, so a good candidate finds a job post and nothing about what working your shifts is like.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted roles recently. Note the roles and which clinics.
openers.linkLine: A careers page for your urgent care clinics: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention x-ray at some clinics, but the site doesn't say which. A parent whose child hurt a wrist needs the nearest walk-in clinic with x-ray, not the nearest one.
openers.hook: Only if they post about x-ray or lab services at specific clinics. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Services filtered by urgent care clinic: {demo-link}

openers.line: School and sports physical season is close, and your clinics don't have a page to book one. Parents book whichever walk-in clinic lets them pick a time.
openers.hook: Use this in the weeks before school terms and sports seasons start. Check if they offer physicals.
openers.linkLine: A sports physical booking page across your clinics: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Virtual visits not on the site
openers.line: Your posts mention video visits, but the site has no way to start one. A patient who'd rather stay home ends up on a national app instead of with your urgent care.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted about virtual or video visits. Check the site for a start button.
openers.linkLine: A virtual visit start page for your clinics: {demo-link}

openers.line: The hours on two of your clinic listings don't match the website. Someone who drives to a closed urgent care clinic remembers it.
openers.hook: Compare listing hours to the site for every clinic. Note the exact mismatch to quote back.
openers.linkLine: Clinic hours kept right everywhere from one place: {demo-link}

openers.line: Several reviews say the care was good but the wait felt endless, mostly because no one knew how long it would be. A text when it's nearly their turn changes how that visit feels.
openers.hook: Find reviews that praise staff but mention waiting. Quote the kindest one back.
openers.linkLine: Wait updates by text for walk-in patients: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're opening a new urgent care clinic in {Neighborhood}. Its page, hours and check-in should be live before the doors open so people find it the first night.
openers.hook: Only if they've announced a new clinic. Note the area and opening date.
openers.linkLine: A launch page for the new walk-in clinic: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your clinic site took a long time to load on my phone's mobile data. Someone feeling unwell in a car park won't wait for it, they'll tap the next urgent care.
openers.hook: Load the site on mobile data, not wifi, and count the seconds. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The urgent care site rebuilt to load fast on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} post from your clinic team was a good reminder that urgent care is local people looking after neighbours. It belongs on the site, not just in a feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest community or team post and name it exactly. Never reference a patient.
openers.linkLine: Your walk-in clinic story on a page people find: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, I was comparing urgent care clinics in {City} on my phone and noticed {Business Name} doesn't show a wait time or let people check in online at any location.

I build sites for walk-in clinic groups: live waits, online check-in, an open-now finder and self-pay prices by clinic. I've sketched a sample for your clinics, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it be useful if I sent it? And should it go to you or to whoever runs operations or marketing?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up on my note about {Business Name}. Here's the sample: {demo-link}

It shows the wait at each clinic, online check-in with a text when it's nearly their turn, an open-now finder, services by clinic, self-pay prices and an employer page. Nothing assesses symptoms, and nothing goes live without your medical director's sign-off. Happy to walk your team through it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for urgent care groups here in {City}. I sent a note a few days ago about wait times and check-in for {Business Name}, did it reach you?"

IF THE CLINIC FRONT DESK ANSWERS:
"No problem, I know you're busy. Who handles the website for all the clinics? I'd like to send them a sample."

IF NO:
"Short version: I built a sample site that shows the wait at each clinic, lets people check in online and lists self-pay prices, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email it to you and your operations lead?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"It's a site the group owns, connected to the check-in and queue system you already run, not a replacement. The build runs {Build Range} depending on clinic count and integrations, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, hours updates and new clinic pages. For your group I'd quote about {Build Price}, phased so check-in goes live first."
"Could we take twenty minutes with you and the medical director this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a phased scope you can share. Phase one is wait times and check-in, and nothing publishes without your sign-off."

objections.objection: Our records system already has online check-in.
objections.handler: "Good, then we put it on the site where patients look. Right now it's hidden behind a menu. The queue stays in your system; the site shows the wait and sends people into it."

objections.objection: Showing wait times will put people off when we're busy.
objections.handler: "They'll see it on someone else's site anyway. A long wait with a text when it's their turn keeps them with you; no number at all sends them to the clinic that shows one."

objections.objection: We can't publish prices; insurance makes it complicated.
objections.handler: "We only publish self-pay ranges you approve, labelled as estimates. Insured patients see which plans each clinic takes. Nothing pretends to be a quote."

objections.objection: Our medical director won't sign off on web content.
objections.handler: "That's the right instinct. Nothing on the site assesses symptoms or gives advice, the emergency guidance is the director's own wording, and they approve every page before launch."

objections.objection: We're part of a bigger brand and marketing is handled centrally.
objections.handler: "Then I'd like to show the central team the sample. Location pages, wait times and employer services are usually where a central site is thinnest."

objections.objection: We're too busy this flu season.
objections.handler: "That's when wait times matter most. Phase one is check-in and live waits, and it needs an hour of your team's time, not a project."
"{Build Range} depending on clinic count and integrations. For your group about {Build Price}, plus {Care Range} a month for hosting, hours updates and new clinic pages."

email.subject: Wait times and check-in for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for urgent care groups in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name} that shows the wait at each clinic and lets people check in online. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking down the wait-time and check-in sample I built for {Business Name}'s clinics on Friday.

Should I keep it up for your operations team to see? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the busy season for walk-in clinics is close and you came to mind.

The sample with live waits and online check-in for {Business Name} is still here, same scope and price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look before the queues start.

bullets: Price the live wait and check-in work as its own line; it's the reason an urgent care group buys.
Count clinics, not pages. Each clinic needs its own hours, services, wait feed and listing kept in step.
Quote the queue-system connection after you've seen it; staff-entered waits cost far less than a live feed.
Build in the medical director's review round; emergency guidance and service lists are theirs to approve.
Sell employer services as a separate phase with its own budget holder, usually operations, not marketing.
Keep self-pay prices as ranges the clinic approves, never a quote, and never any claim about outcomes.

lineItems.description: Max with its own services filter, hours by day, parking and access notes, insurance list and check-in button.
Max when waits come straight from the clinic's queue system for every location rather than staff updates.
Max with a held place in the real queue, texts as their turn nears and privacy-safe storage of the check-in details.
Max when prices differ by clinic or service bundle and include tests, x-ray and procedures.
Max with service selection, billing details, authorised contacts and routing to the occupational health lead.
Max when it hands patients into their video visit system with hours, pricing and a clear in-person fallback.
Max when every clinic page, the check-in and the emergency guidance are translated and checked by fluent staff.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile hours and wait posts for every clinic
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every urgent care clinic's profile kept exact: holiday hours, services, the check-in link and a short weekly post, so nobody drives to a clinic that's closed."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the clinic pages are live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Post-visit review requests, privacy-checked
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Walk-in patients who leave happy are the ones least likely to post. A text the next morning asks how that urgent care clinic did, worded so it never names why they came in."

whatElseYouSell.name: Flu-shot and school physical campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Landing pages, profile posts and clinic signage for flu-shot season and school physicals, each pointing to check-in at the nearest urgent care clinic."

whatElseYouSell.name: Advertising-approval-ready urgent care content pack
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Before a flu-shot or work-injury campaign runs, its urgent care copy is stripped of speed and outcome promises and filed as a ready-to-submit pack, for places where the regulator approves health ads first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Health-data hosting and form setup for check-in
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Online check-in collects names, birth dates and insurance details. I set up the urgent care hosting, encryption and staff access for that data and hand your privacy lead a written record of how it's done."

whatElseYouSell.name: Consent and patient-photo policy pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Policy pages and consent forms for any testimonial or photo, so every clinic manager knows what can be posted and what needs a signature first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Accessibility review of clinic pages and check-in
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Someone with low vision or a shaking hand still needs to check in at a walk-in clinic. I test the wait board and check-in with assistive tools, fix what fails and publish an accessibility statement."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, or before an employer contract asks for it.

whatElseYouSell.name: Employer outreach kit for occupational health
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page service sheet, an employer landing page and a short email sequence for HR managers near each clinic, so occupational health stops relying on word of mouth."

whatElseYouSell.name: Clinic team portrait days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short shoot at each clinic of the providers, nurses and front desk, so the location pages show the people a worried patient will actually meet. No patients in frame."

withoutAI.route: Physical therapy clinics that take sprain referrals
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The physio clinics your urgent care sends sprains and strains to need booking pages of their own. An introduction from a clinic that refers them patients carries weight."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Therapy clinics live on referrals, and a busy walk-in network is one of their best sources.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pharmacies across the road from your clinics fill your patients' prescriptions every night. A site with refill requests and late hours is overdue for most of them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pharmacists know the clinic staff by name and trust their recommendation.

withoutAI.route: Imaging centres that take the group's scan referrals
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your providers send someone for an MRI or ultrasound, the imaging centre's booking page is the next step. A word from the urgent care makes the introduction easy."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Imaging centres compete for referring clinics, so they listen to one that sends them patients.

withoutAI.route: Primary care practices that take follow-ups
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Patients without a family doctor ask your clinic staff where to go next. The practices you suggest need a new-patient page that's open and clear."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Family practices value the steady flow of new patients a walk-in network sends them.

withoutAI.route: Youth sports leagues that send players for physicals
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The leagues whose players come to your clinics for sports physicals run registration on paper and group chats. A league site with sign-up and forms suits them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Leagues are grateful to the clinic that handles their physicals and take its recommendation.

withoutAI.route: Small employers on the occupational health account
withoutAI.whoPays: Each employer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The contractors and warehouses that send workers to your clinic often have a weak site themselves. Your occupational health manager can mention me at the next account review."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Employers trust the clinic network that looks after their staff and take its suggestions seriously.

withAI.route: Injury intake assistant for physical therapy clinics
withAI.pitchLine: "Patients referred from urgent care answer an assistant's intake questions before their first physio visit, and the therapist gets a tidy summary. It never assesses the injury."
withAI.whyItWorks: Therapists start the first session with the history ready, and referred patients book faster.

withAI.route: Refill and hours assistant for pharmacies
withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant answers refill status, late hours and stock questions from the pharmacy's own system, and passes anything about medicines to the pharmacist."
withAI.whyItWorks: Pharmacists spend hours on the phone with questions the system already knows the answer to.

withAI.route: Referral scheduling assistant for imaging centres
withAI.pitchLine: "When a clinic referral arrives, an assistant offers the patient times by text and sends the scan's prep sheet, so the imaging slot is booked before they forget."
withAI.whyItWorks: Every referral booked quickly is one the centre doesn't lose to a competitor.

withAI.route: Work-injury paperwork helper for employers' HR
withAI.pitchLine: "HR teams fill in the same injury and return-to-work forms every time. An assistant drafts them from details the employer already holds, for HR to check and file."
withAI.whyItWorks: Paperwork is the slow part of every work injury, and the clinic looks helpful for the introduction.

withAI.route: Registration and forms reminders for sports leagues
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents get reminders for missing registration and physical forms, and coaches see who's cleared to play, with a link to book a sports physical at the clinic."
withAI.whyItWorks: Leagues hate chasing forms, and the clinic gets the physicals booked.

withAI.route: New-patient booking assistant for family practices
withAI.pitchLine: "Patients sent on from urgent care can ask whether the family practice is taking new patients and book a first appointment, without waiting on hold."
withAI.whyItWorks: Practices fill their open new-patient slots, and the clinic's follow-up advice actually happens.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with the nearest open clinic
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call to any urgent care clinic gets a text with the current wait at the nearest open clinic and a check-in link, plus a note to call the emergency number if it's serious."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs each clinic's number forwarded and wording the medical director approves.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that never confirm a visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clinic managers get a suggested response to every new urgent care review, polite about the wait if it was long and careful never to reveal that the writer was a patient."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few approved replies and their privacy rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Follow-up booking texts after a visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients the provider asks to come back get a text with a link to book that recheck at the same urgent care clinic, instead of being told to call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a follow-up flag from their records system and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Self-pay estimates and online payment
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Self-pay patients see an estimate for their kind of clinic visit before they come and pay the balance online after, with a receipt they can submit to their insurer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their self-pay price list and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Hiring pipeline for nurses and providers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every applicant for every urgent care clinic lands on one board by role and location, so managers see who applied and who is waiting on an interview."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their roles, interview steps and which managers hire for which clinic.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for nurse, provider and x-ray roles
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants answer the group's questions on licence, shift preferences and which clinic suits them, and managers get a short summary of who fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, with the hiring pipeline. Needs must-haves per role. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Website assistant for hours, prices and clinic services
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'which clinic has x-ray open now' and 'what does a self-pay visit cost' from your own pages. It never assesses symptoms and points anything serious to the emergency number."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs approved prices and services by clinic, plus the medical director's sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Insurance card capture at check-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients snap their insurance card during online check-in, the details are read into the form, and the front desk confirms them before the walk-in visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after check-in is live. Needs privacy review and their records system fields. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Employer portal for occupational health accounts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Employers authorise a worker's visit, see the work-status form once it's signed and download invoices, without calling the clinic."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their occupational health workflow, consent rules and billing setup.

softwareAI.name: Signed work-status form delivery
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Once the provider signs a work-status form, it goes to the employer's authorised contact automatically, with the worker's consent recorded at the clinic."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, with the employer portal. Needs consent wording and each employer's contacts.

softwareAI.name: Work-status form drafts for provider sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a work injury visit, the provider gets a draft work-status form from their own visit note to check and sign, instead of filling it from scratch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their form templates and a privacy review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; providers sign every form.

softwareAI.name: Provider shift board across clinics
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every provider, nurse and x-ray shift at every urgent care clinic on one board, with open shifts offered to staff by text."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their rota rules, roles and which staff work which clinics.

softwareAI.name: Staffing forecast from visit history
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Past visit counts by hour, season and clinic turn into a suggested rota for the weeks ahead, so the walk-in rush isn't met by a skeleton crew."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs a year of visit counts by clinic and the shift board. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Call summaries for the central phone line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls to the group's line, recorded with consent, get a short summary and a task for the right clinic, so a callback about a result or a bill doesn't slip."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs call recording with consent notices and phone system access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Virtual visit queue and booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients join a video visit queue from the site, see their place in line, and the clinic's providers take them between walk-ins."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs their video visit system, provider hours and the rules where each clinic practises.

softwareAI.name: Multilingual check-in and reminder drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Check-in prompts and wait texts are drafted in the patient's language and checked by fluent staff, so families who speak another language at home use the walk-in clinic confidently."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, where staff can review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Results-ready notices that link to the portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a lab or x-ray result is ready, the patient gets a text saying so, with no details, and a link to sign in and see it once a provider has reviewed it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, with the patient portal. Needs result status from their records system and privacy sign-off.

softwareAI.name: Clinic performance dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Check-ins, walk-outs, time from arrival to discharge and review counts for each urgent care clinic on one screen, so operations sees where the queue is breaking."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs three months of queue and visit data from each clinic.

softwareAI.name: Visit note drafts from provider dictation
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Between walk-ins, a provider speaks the encounter aloud and an urgent care chart note is drafted in the clinic's template, waiting for them to correct and sign before it enters the record."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 10. Needs note templates, patient consent wording and a privacy review. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Patient portal for visit summaries and receipts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Patients sign in to see their clinic visit summary, reviewed results, receipts and school or work notes, in the group's own brand."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs deep records-system integration, payment setup and a full privacy review.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise live waits and check-in for other urgent care groups
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Urgent care groups, monthly per clinic
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The wait board, check-in and open-now finder I built for one urgent care group work for any walk-in network, loaded with their own clinics."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first group paid for the queue connection; the next ones need only their clinics and brand.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The urgent care association, as a member benefit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a clinic site template with wait times, careful emergency guidance and privacy-safe check-in already built."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations run on member benefits, and small clinic owners keep asking them about websites.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The hospital system's ambulatory or marketing team
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your walk-in clinics sit behind the hospital's main site with no live waits. A dedicated urgent care front door takes pressure off the emergency department."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hospitals want minor cases steered away from the emergency department, and they budget centrally.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency runs ads for urgent care groups but can't build live waits or check-in. I deliver it under your name."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship and lack the integration skills, so a white-label build lets them keep the account.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Employer associations buying occupational health access
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your members need one place to send injured workers. A member portal linked to partner clinics makes that a benefit you can advertise."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations sell access, and a clinic network with a portal gives them a concrete member perk.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pharmacy group running in-store clinics
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your in-store walk-in clinics need the same live waits and check-in as a standalone urgent care, inside the pharmacy's brand."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The product is already built for walk-in queues; only the brand and services change.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pet owners choose a vet urgent care exactly as people choose a walk-in clinic: wait and distance. The same wait board and check-in fit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A different industry with the identical queue problem, and few builders serve it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The management company running clinics for physician owners
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You run several walk-in clinics for different owners. One platform for waits, check-in and location pages, billed per clinic you manage."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Management companies want one system across owners, and they add clinics steadily.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every new franchise clinic needs its page, waits and check-in on opening day. I set them up from one template as each one opens."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchisors want consistent launches, and each opening repeats the same work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The medical teams at stadiums and festivals need a booking site for organisers and a staff shift page. Your clinicians who work events can introduce me."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Event medics often staff from urgent care rotas, so the introduction comes naturally.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One urgent care group per metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An urgent care group in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build wait boards and check-in for one walk-in clinic group per metro. Your competitors in {City} won't get the same setup from me."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups value not sharing a builder with a direct rival, and the build carries over to the next metro.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The clinic group with a half-built check-in
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your check-in project stalled when the vendor or developer moved on. I can finish it on a structure already running at other urgent care clinics."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These groups have already decided and budgeted; they need someone who can finish.

upsellLadder.offer: Urgent care site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: Operations and the medical director approve phase one: waits, check-in and clinic pages.
upsellLadder.line: "The urgent care site and care plan sit on one contract, so a holiday hours change or a new clinic page is a message to me, not a project."

upsellLadder.offer: Google profile hours and wait posts for every clinic
upsellLadder.trigger: Check-ins start arriving from the site, and a clinic listing still shows the wrong hours.
upsellLadder.line: "Patients are checking in from the site. Keeping every clinic's profile exact sends more of them there."

upsellLadder.offer: Missed-call text-back with the nearest open clinic
upsellLadder.trigger: Phone logs show unanswered calls during the evening rush.
upsellLadder.line: "Your clinics miss calls in the evening rush. A text with the nearest wait and a check-in link keeps those patients."

upsellLadder.trigger: Flu-shot season or school physical season is a few weeks away.
upsellLadder.line: "Flu-shot season is close. A page and posts that send people to check in at the nearest clinic will fill the quiet hours."

upsellLadder.offer: Employer portal for occupational health accounts
upsellLadder.trigger: Employer account requests start arriving through the form, and staff are emailing work-status forms by hand.
upsellLadder.line: "Employers are signing up through the site. A portal lets them see signed forms and invoices without calling your clinics."

upsellLadder.trigger: Another clinic opens, or managers mention filling shifts by group text.
upsellLadder.line: "With another clinic open, shifts by group text won't hold. One board for every urgent care rota will."

upsellLadder.trigger: Providers have quiet stretches between walk-ins, or patients ask about video visits in reviews.
upsellLadder.line: "Your providers have gaps between walk-ins. A virtual visit queue fills them without anyone leaving home."

upsellLadder.trigger: The annual review, when operations asks which clinics lose patients to the wait.
upsellLadder.line: "A year in, let's see where walk-in patients leave before being seen and fix the clinics where the queue breaks."
